content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.33) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment ≤ 0.33) — model is overly optimistic, fails to reflect bearish momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then drifts toward historical mean — correct by smoothing out extreme deviations.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in price correction — model often misses early downward trends, especially after sentiment shifts to negative.
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., 0.00 or negative), model should reduce forecast volatility and avoid upward revisions — avoid “rebound” overcorrection.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model should not assume continuation — adjust downward bias to reflect sentiment decay.
- Model overfits recent highs — when sentiment is positive and price peaks, forecast should not assume further rise — cap upward revisions at 1–2% above recent peak.
